body:
## Problem

In the v2 compiler workflow we regularly need both a fast edit-time debug build and an occasional release/O3 build for benchmark and scaling gates. Right now changing the Simple C++ build mode effectively invalidates the active build tree, so Ninja cannot keep both configurations hot.

Recent measured example from the compiler v2 workflow:

- debug build: 455.59s
- release/O3 build: 707.98s

Those times are acceptable for a cold configuration build, but the painful part is the mode switch. If we run an O3 benchmark, the normal debug/edit build is no longer hot; switching back costs another large rebuild instead of a cheap no-change Ninja pass. This discourages using O3 only as a measurement gate, because one benchmark can burn the next edit cycle too.

## Requested Direction

Please separate debug and release build products so each mode has its own persistent Ninja/object/binary output tree.

The important behavior we want:

1. Build debug once.
2. Build release/O3 once.
3. Re-run debug with no source changes and get a cheap no-change build.
4. Re-run release/O3 with no source changes and get a cheap no-change build.
5. Switching modes should select a different already-built tree, not overwrite/invalidate the previous one.

Possible shape:

- `.prism/build/debug/...`
- `.prism/build/release/...`
- separate generated/native object directories per build mode when flags affect compilation
- separate final executable paths per build mode
- mode-specific Ninja metadata/deps files
- clean commands that can clean one mode or all modes

Generated source can remain shared only if it is truly independent of build mode. Anything affected by compiler flags, defines, optimization/debug flags, target ABI, sanitizer flags, or profile settings should be mode-keyed.

## Why This Matters

For the compiler project we are intentionally separating validation into gates:

- edit-time: focused checks, no rebuild when possible
- batch gate: one shared build
- measurement gate: release/O3/scaling only when performance-relevant

That procedure only works well if the measurement gate does not destroy the hot edit-time build. Otherwise a single O3 run costs the O3 build plus the next debug rebuild.

## Acceptance Criteria

A good result would be:

- `scpp build` in debug mode writes to a debug-specific build tree and executable.
- `scpp build` in release/O3 mode writes to a release-specific build tree and executable.
- Switching debug -> release -> debug with no source changes leaves the second debug build as a Ninja no-change/minimal build.
- Switching release -> debug -> release with no source changes leaves the second release build as a Ninja no-change/minimal build.
- Build artifacts, object files, generated depfiles, profile/debug reports, and final executables do not cross-contaminate between modes.
- The selected executable path is discoverable by scripts, so benchmark runners can intentionally pick debug or release.

## Nice To Have

- CLI override such as `--mode debug|release` or an environment override, in addition to config-file mode.
- Optional build-root suffix/key for future variants such as sanitizers or profile-guided builds.
- A small smoke test that builds debug, builds release, then checks that returning to debug does not trigger a full rebuild.

This would let us keep normal development fast while still running O3 benchmarks responsibly.
title: Separate debug and release build trees so Ninja can keep both hot
